title: The divine argument: Word, signs, and senses; Moses and Aaron; Christ the legate of legates
pass_a_gloss: XV. The divine argument by which the Holy Spirit through His envoys persuades people that what they put forward is without fail God's Word — and that all sufficiently offered it must take it as God's Word, so that those who refuse stand condemned as unbelievers — holds three elements: first the Word itself spoken by God or by some envoy in God's name; second sure signs and witnesses by which people not altogether stubborn are brought to grant that this is from God; third eyes, ears, sense and reason, by which both Word and signs are taken in. 1. When God sent Moses and Aaron He supplied them with Word and signs, yet had already supplied His people with sense and intellect (Exod. 4.30; 19.9); therefore Israel gladly took Moses' word as divine (Deut. 5.27). 2. Those signs worked not only among eyewitnesses (autōptai) but among later generations who have the fathers' history and tradition in place of seeing for themselves (Ps. 44.2; 78.2; Deut. 4.9-10). 3. Other prophets followed Moses with like authority, agreeing with the sacred letters already finished and pressing that no new worship be taken up. 4. The envoy of envoys, Apostle and High Priest of our confession, is JESUS CHRIST, whom Moses foretold (Deut. 18.15). Witnesses: sacred letters (John 5.39, 46; Luke 24.46; Acts 10.43); John the Baptist; the voice from heaven; miracles; resurrection; ascension. The Apostles followed Christ.
pass_b_english: XV. The divine argument by which the Holy Spirit through His legates persuades humans that what they propose is infallibly God's Word — which all to whom it is sufficiently proposed must receive as God's Word, so that those who do not are condemned as unbelievers — contains three things: (1) the Word itself, which God or some legate in God's name has spoken; (2) certain signs and testimonies by which humans not wholly obstinate are persuaded this is from God; (3) eyes, ears, sense and reason, by which they can infallibly perceive that Word and those signs.

1. When God sent Moses and Aaron, He gave them the Word and signs, but had already given sense and intellect to His people ([[Exodus 4:30 >> Bible:Exodus 4:30]]; [[Exodus 19:9 >> Bible:Exodus 19:9]]). Therefore Israel gladly embraced Moses' word as divine ([[Deuteronomy 5:27 >> Bible:Deuteronomy 5:27]]).

2. Those signs were efficacious not only among eyewitnesses (αὐτόπται) but among posterity, who have fathers' history and tradition instead of autopsy ([[Psalm 44:2 >> Bible:Psalm 44:2]]; [[Psalm 78:2 >> Bible:Psalm 78:2]]; [[Deuteronomy 4:9 >> Bible:Deuteronomy 4:9]]-[[Deuteronomy 4:10 >> Bible:Deuteronomy 4:10]]).
3. Other prophets followed Moses with equal authority, agreeing with the sacred letters already complete and pressing that no new worship be received.

4. The legate of legates, Apostle and High Priest of our confession, is JESUS CHRIST, whom Moses foretold ([[Deuteronomy 18:15 >> Bible:Deuteronomy 18:15]]). Testimony: sacred letters ([[John 5:39 >> Bible:John 5:39]], [[John 5:46 >> Bible:John 5:46]]; [[Luke 24:46 >> Bible:Luke 24:46]]; [[Acts 10:43 >> Bible:Acts 10:43]]); John the Baptist ([[John 1:7 >> Bible:John 1:7]]); God's voice from heaven ([[Matthew 3:17 >> Bible:Matthew 3:17]]; [[Matthew 17:5 >> Bible:Matthew 17:5]]; [[2 Peter 1:16 >> Bible:2 Peter 1:16]]); miracles ([[John 5:36 >> Bible:John 5:36]]; [[John 10:25 >> Bible:John 10:25]]); resurrection ([[Romans 1:4 >> Bible:Romans 1:4]]); ascension ([[Luke 24:51 >> Bible:Luke 24:51]]; [[Acts 1:9 >> Bible:Acts 1:9]]). As prophets followed Moses, so the Apostles followed Christ.
source_text: XV. Argumentum divinum tria continet: 1. verbum ipsum; 2. signa & testimonia certa; 3. sensus & ratio. Exemplo Mosis & Aaronis (Exod. 4.30; Deut. 5.27). Signa efficacia apud αὐτόπτας & posteros. Prophetae Mosen secuti. Legatus legatorum est JESUS CHRISTUS (Deut. 18.15); Apostoli Christum secuti.
